versions.changelog: Add end-of-run 'report platform friction' feedback step (fb_8s2h7m87tg).

- No functional or procedural changes; documentation (SKILL.md) was reformatted or edited for clarity.
- All instructions and categories remain unchanged.
- No changes to user-facing features or workflow.

**Broader extraction: Problems can now be inspired by a paper, not just those it explicitly states.**

- Problems may be sourced from issues the paper explicitly raises or genuinely open questions it inspires in a knowledgeable reader, as long as the connection is clearly motivated by the paper.
- Updated instructions throughout SKILL.md to clarify "springboard" approach; not limited to paper-authored problem statements.
- Guidance added to explain how to handle inspired problems, including how to document the link in problem descriptions.
- No changes to the taxonomy or technical workflow; de-duplication and publishing steps are unchanged.
- Minor documentation and rubric clarifications; removed deprecated skill-card.md file.

- Added support for topic-focused mining: you can now optionally specify a keyword when fetching un-mined literature to restrict mining to papers relevant to a particular topic.
- Updated the procedure to describe how to use the new "keyword" parameter for targeted backlog processing.
- Clarified user instructions for topic-based and global backlog mining.
- Removed obsolete documentation file skill-card.md.

**This release expands problem categories and improves deduplication workflow.**

- Adds a 4-category taxonomy: scientific, technical, theoretical, methodological; allows at most one problem per category per paper.
- Candidate extraction now considers each category independently, with a high bar for inclusion.
- Deduplication step now links to existing problems via `link_problem_literature` (replacing attention bumping).
- Updated publish logic: `kind` must exactly match one of the four allowed values.
- Reporting now includes category info and which problems were linked versus newly published.
- Removed outdated/duplicate files (e.g., `skill-card.md`).
dedup now bumps the matched problem's attention_count (independent re-derivation signal)

Initial release: mine scientific/technical research problems from un-mined literature over MCP, one paper per run (read full text -> extract candidates -> de-duplicate against existing problems -> publish survivors -> mark mined).
